packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-10 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (listed the packet directory and read image dimensions with sips, did not open packet.json).

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001.jpg; face A)
- Upright parchment strip, roughly 13 x 33 cm by the scale, cut from a larger sheet. Single block of text, long lines, in a German-language vernacular cursive (Kanzlei-type) hand, dark brown ink. Not a codex column: it reads like documentary prose (a charter/deed or register entry), with comma-like virgulae and periods.
- The left edge of the writing is preserved (left margin about 1/3 of the strip width, blank except for marks); the right edge is cut, so every line is truncated on the right. About 36-37 lines visible, top line partly cut at the top edge.
- A vertical fold/crease runs through the strip near the left of the text block (about at x=930 in the overview).
- Enlarged flourished initials (looped strokes) jut into the left margin at overview lines ~13-14 ("Wer"/"Mer"?) and ~35-36 ("Und"?), plus a smaller one at line ~17. Large looped capitals also inside lines (e.g. top right "Wer/Mer", line 6 "Item"?). Faint offset/ghost letters in the left margin near the top (mirror-image?), a red-brown stain at left margin around line 12-13, a "11"/"ll" mark in the margin.
- Modern pencil shelfmark at bottom: "Stams, STA, Frag. 61 r(?)" [reading of pencil note tentative].
- No rubrics, no running titles, no glosses visible.
- Tiles image-002..007 = 2 columns x 3 rows of this face at native resolution, overlapping. Face B overview is image-008, tiles image-009..014.

CONVENTIONS: The hand uses a Kanzlei "M" that looks like "az"/"a3" with a hook; I transcribe it as M. u-superscripts (circle/o or two strokes over u) given as ů/ü as seen. Virgula "/" and comma-like strokes rendered as "," or "/"; periods as ".". Word division as seen where I can.

Running text across 004/005 (my joining, same physical lines): "...Namblich viertzehen Mu[tmal]... gůtter und Zehend, besůchts und unbesůchts, zu Dorff ... haben, nichts davon ausgeschlossen ... handlen, thuen und lassen als all[...] Erben und Nachkhomen sollen auch [...]khomen als Lehen und Grunther[r] ... oder [...] nit gestatten. Sunder verkauffen wolten oder mu[sten?] menigclichen nach Lanndsrecht..."

Pencil (lower left of tile): "[Fr]g. 61 r" - reads as "61r".
Face A summary: about 37 written lines (incl. cut top line), all cut on the right. Read all visible line-beginnings and line-portions across the six tiles; nothing left unread on face A apart from the cut-off right portions (lost) and words noted as uncertain.

=====================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY, FACE B (overview image-008.jpg)
- Same strip, other side (pencil at bottom "Stams, STA, Frag. 61 v?"). The strip is shown with the text-side features mirrored relative to face A (fold now right of centre-left at x~925).
- Main visible writing: a large title-label in black textura/Fraktur-style display letters, three lines, with a big flourished initial D: "Der diener und / Ehalten Ge- / dinng" with diamond-point ornaments either side of line 3, and below, spaced large numerals "· 1 5 5 0 ·" with point ornaments. This looks like a later label/cover title written when the strip was reused (tentative interpretation: wrapper or spine label of a volume/register).
- Below and behind the title: faint brown cursive lines across most of the strip. These appear to be show-through (mirror image) of the face-A text, judging from the layout matching face A; to be checked on tiles.
- Horizontal crease lines (near top at y~265, middle y~520, lower y~740, and y~940) and a vertical fold; a small round stain near bottom; pen-strokes "· ' ' ///" in the right margin at overview y~420-530 (unclear marks, possibly pen trials or tally strokes).

--- image-009.jpg (face B, upper-left tile) ---
Title (black display script, large):
T1  [initial D with long flourish] Der dien[er ...]
T2  Ehalte[n ...]  (written "Eehalt.." / "Echalt..")
T3  [·] dinn[g ...]
Date:  ·1 5 [5 0]  (large numerals with point ornament at left)
IMPORTANT OBSERVATION: the faint brown cursive behind the title is NOT mirror-reversed in this image; it reads in normal direction and its wording repeats face-A wording, in the same line order. Its line-starts sit at the left edge of this face (x~120-560 of the tile), i.e. in the left part of the strip. I cannot tell from the images whether this is show-through photographed oddly, an offset, or a second (erased/faded) copy written on this face; I record only what is legible. Faint lines, top to bottom (y = approx pixel row in this tile):

These faint readings support the face-A readings "Mülinner", "Sechs Mutmal daselbs", "Claus", "weiß? daselbs", "-hofers Erben gůt". Small red-brown stains top left.

Full title as read from 009+010: "Der diener und / Ehalten Ge- / dinng(?)" and below "1 5 5 0".
Faint cursive lines only in the left third of this tile (next to the fold), too faint to read beyond scattered letters ("[...]nnd", "[...]ben", "an des"?). =====================================================================
SUMMARY AND LIMITATIONS
- Face A (images 001-007): one block of ~37 lines of German documentary prose in a vernacular cursive (Kanzlei-type) hand; left margin preserved, every line cut on the right, so only the left ~60-70% of each line survives. Content as read: field/property descriptions with boundaries ("Mittag", "gegen mitternacht", "an gemainem weg", "an gemainen Waal", "Erben gůt"), measures ("Mütt Traid", "Mutmal"), named persons ("Melchior Gottsch?", "Claus Grop?", "Crysten P..."), places ("Mülinner", "Burgeis?", "Mall[s]?", "Sannt Maria perg?"), then a tenure clause ("gůtter und Zehend, besůchts und unbesůchts ... nichts davon ausgeschlossen ... Erben und Nachkhomen ... als Lehen und Grunther[r] ... nit gestatten ... verkauffen ... nach Lanndsrecht ... als Lehentrager ... auff Sannt Martins ... auf ainen Jeden Sannd Galle? ... zinns, Namblich Sechshund... als offt ain Lehentrager abge[...] ... entgeltnus ... Lehenherrn zuthuen sch[uldig] ... nach dem Lanndsrechten"). These are my readings of the letters only; I have not tried to identify the document.
- Face B (images 008-014): a later display-script label "Der diener und / Ehalten Ge- / dinng(?)" and the numerals "1550", plus faint brown cursive behind it that is non-mirrored and repeats face-A wording in the same line order; I could not determine whether it is show-through, offset, or a faded second copy. Its readings corroborate several face-A words.
- Most uncertain words: L3 "[...]ganot", L5 "an wisen", L6 "Stiftung", L8 "Ackhern in Khu-", L14 "pawen des Clau..", the surname in L18 "M..schofers", "Prugg?ls", "Sennen Lehenzinser", 004/005 L14 first word, "Crysten P.r.ü.", "Galle/Balle", "In wunser der", "unverrenblich", final line "[...]gnachtes gebürdte".
- Lost: right-hand portions of every face-A line (physically cut away). Nothing further to read on available images; a raking-light or UV image of face B might clarify the faint layer.
- Line numbering: image-002 and image-003 share one numbering (003 has an extra cut line L0 at top); images 004-007 are numbered from the top of each image, with overlaps marked.
